long_biography.plain_text:
Chairing Australia's Financial Centre Task Force placed Mark Johnson AO at the centre of a national effort to make the country's financial system more competitive and internationally connected. He continued that policy work through Asia-Pacific business bodies, bringing the perspective of a banker who had helped develop Australia's merchant-banking market.

Johnson joined Hill Samuel Australia as joint managing director in 1971, when the young firm was building its advisory and markets capabilities. After founding and running Australian Bank, he returned to the business that became Macquarie, eventually serving as deputy chairman. He later chaired infrastructure and energy companies and remains a senior adviser in corporate finance.
